correctness.rationale: The group-scheme coordinates are the gap-indexed coefficients of the negative logarithmic derivative. They are invariant under both gluing-unit actions and form an additive polynomial coordinate system by triangularity and invertibility of every gap modulo p. The full alpha_p coaction follows from the chain rule and Newton/Frobenius identities; the infinitesimal fixed ideal is exactly (w_g for g>=p, w_1^p,...,w_(p-2)^p). Jensen splitting as stated in Fong–Maccan–Modin Corollary 5.2 transfers the computation to the surface. Exact independent formal-arithmetic checks passed for p=3,5,7,11,13; these checks do not replace the all-prime proof.

originality.rationale: Fong–Maccan–Modin, arXiv:2611.12201, Remark 5.9 identifies this full fixed-point group-scheme determination as an unresolved direction, after determining the underlying additive curve Picard group and the tangent dimension p-2. The new exact coaction and fixed ideal determine height, nilpotence and length for all p>=5. Hilario–Schröer arXiv:2303.12324 construct the curve and action without this Picard fixed subgroup. The p=3 case is expressly identified as prior, not new.

value.rationale: The exact structure resolves the explicitly identified p>=5 group-scheme gap: it supplies the nonreduced coordinate algebra, height one and length p^(p-2), rather than the preexisting tangent dimension p-2. Nonisomorphic infinitesimal group schemes can share tangent dimensions, so this is a genuinely informative geometric classification with applications to torsors and Picard deformation behavior.
